schema_version.description: Configuration format. Accepts 1 only. Other versions fail startup rather than being silently migrated.

host.description: Listen address. Accepts 127.0.0.1 or ::1. Chooses IPv4 or IPv6 loopback behind the TLS proxy.

port.description: TCP port. Accepts 1–65535 in deployed configurations. Use a free port distinct from the other listener.

allowed_hosts.description: Exact accepted Host headers. Accepts host:port strings, including the reverse proxy public authority. Other hosts are rejected to prevent DNS rebinding.

items.description: Accepted authority. Accepts a hostname with optional port or bracketed IPv6 with port. Matching is case-insensitive and exact.

origins.description: Browser origins. Accepts exact scheme://host[:port] strings, or an empty list. Empty rejects all browser Origin headers but permits native clients without Origin.

items.description: Allowed Origin. Accepts one exact HTTP or HTTPS origin without a trailing slash. Only this origin receives CORS access.

business.description: Business listener configuration. Accepts the specified loopback host, port, Host and Origin fields. Controls REST and MCP ingress.

control.description: Control listener configuration. Accepts the specified loopback host, port, Host and Origin fields. Keeps health and metrics independent of business capacity.

clients.description: Client credentials. Accepts 1–100 client objects. Each unique ID and secret define a separate cache identity.

id.description: Client identity. Accepts 1–64 letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen. Distinct IDs isolate cached pages.

token_env.description: Credential environment variable. Accepts a nonempty variable name. The value is loaded at startup without storing it in JSON.

token_file.description: Credential file. Accepts a protected absolute or config-relative path. Read once at startup, so restart applies rotation.

url.description: Fixed SearXNG JSON endpoint. Accepts HTTP for trusted local deployment or HTTPS. Tool arguments can never change this destination.

token_env.description: Credential environment variable. Accepts a nonempty variable name. The value is loaded at startup without storing it in JSON.

token_file.description: Credential file. Accepts a protected absolute or config-relative path. Read once at startup, so restart applies rotation.

ca_file.description: Backend CA file. Accepts an empty string for system trust or a config-relative/absolute PEM path. A supplied bundle changes backend trust only.

engines.description: Requested upstream engines. Accepts one to twenty configured SearXNG engine names. All named engines failing produces provider_unavailable.

items.description: Engine identifier. Accepts a configured SearXNG name. Unknown names cannot produce results.

provider.description: Search provider configuration. Accepts one fixed SearXNG endpoint plus optional credential and CA source. Changes require restart.

directory.description: Disposable state directory. Accepts a config-relative or absolute path. Cache files are created here and must not be shared between running instances.

max_bytes.description: Total cache file budget. Accepts 16 MiB–1 TiB, default 256 MiB. Includes database and journal reserve, so payload capacity is lower.

max_entries.description: Maximum cached records. Accepts 1–1000000, default 10000. Smaller limits evict older entries sooner.

search_ttl_seconds.description: Search cache lifetime. Accepts 1–86400 seconds, default 1800. Partial results are kept at most 30 seconds, and partial results without any hits are not cached.

page_ttl_seconds.description: Page snapshot lifetime. Accepts 1–86400 seconds, default 1800. Expired page IDs can no longer be opened or searched.

cache.description: Cache limits. Accepts directory, byte/entry budgets and TTLs. All cached content remains scoped to client identity.

max_concurrent.description: Business request capacity. Accepts 1–64, default 5. Excess requests immediately receive busy instead of waiting in an unbounded queue.

search_timeout_seconds.description: Search deadline. Accepts 1–60 seconds, default 15. Covers all upstream pages of one call without retries; hits from earlier pages are returned as partial when a later page runs out of time.

open_timeout_seconds.description: Page download deadline. Accepts 1–60 seconds, default 20. Covers DNS, redirects and transfer.

limits.description: Request limits. Accepts concurrency and end-to-end deadlines. Higher limits increase memory and upstream load.
